disposition_reason: Review of selenium metabolic pathways and metabolites; mechanistic context, no occurrence data.

study.design: narrative review of selenium metabolism from speciation studies
study.method: not applicable (review of HPLC-ICP-MS speciation work)

non_numeric_findings: Body contains around 10 mg selenium per 60 kg body weight (p. 107).
Adequate range between deficient and excessive doses in experimental animals spans about one order of magnitude, 0.1 to 1.0 ug/g diet or mL drinking water (p. 107).
Selenite and selenate are reduced to selenide; selenomethionine is converted to selenocysteine by trans-selenation, then lysed to selenide (Abstract).
Surplus selenium is methylated; major urinary metabolite is a selenosugar; trimethylselenonium has been proposed as a marker of excessive dose but recent results contradict this (Abstract).
